sampleContent: All station, artist and track names in these concepts are illustrative.

concepts.name: Rooftop selector
concepts.distinction: A compact station rail keeps browsing beside a large selected-station stage.
concepts.direction: ROOFTOP SELECTOR. Desktop has a slim global icon/nav rail, then a 250px-wide station directory with search and six compact rows, then one generous selected-station stage filling remaining width. The stage has large fresh anime rooftop DJ artwork on its top 60%, and a cool-gray information band below with huge upright "Night Ride", modest genres and two artist seeds. Active Night Ride row has acid edge. Keep all six stations visible. The bottom player spans the stage only, visually unified with its content. The artwork is acid-sky, cobalt brutalist rooftops, orange cables, original anime DJ sitting beside speaker stacks on the RIGHT, leaving title breathing room. Mobile: intentionally stack a clipped edge-to-edge art crop, large Night Ride title, restrained seeds, bottom waveform+playback; a small station-switcher text button near back nav. Light functional panels with ink framing. Balanced, approachable, unmistakable Lyra.
concepts.risk: Balanced browsing and listening; artwork should not crowd the station rail.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-fidelity finished UI concept board for Lyra, an anime street-radio music app. Landscape 3:2 board, ideally 2400 x 1600 or higher resolution. Show two FLAT front-on interface screenshots on a restrained neutral ink presentation canvas: a LARGE landscape DESKTOP radio directory at left, approximately 75% of the board width, and a legible tall MOBILE station-detail screen at right, approximately 23%. No perspective device render, no captions outside the interfaces; the real comparison gallery will supply number/name. Both screenshots must be complete, carefully composed, readable, with intentional whitespace. This is a real radio application concept, not a mood board.
REFERENCE ROLES: Image 1 is the actual Lyra brand board: preserve its original LYRA graffiti mark, expressive condensed display typography resembling Barlow Condensed, readable Space Grotesk UI, acid/cobalt/orange/ink world. Its old cream swatch is superseded by COOL gray #f3f4f6 and #e4e7ec. Image 2 is the actual BEFORE screenshot for feature inventory only: reinterpret its layout radically according to this concept, do not copy its banner/row composition. Image 3 is the original anime rooftop artwork as a visual-treatment reference: original illustrated urban skaters/DJs, cell shading, screenprint grain, concrete and big graffiti strokes. Create coherent fresh artwork for this direction, not videogame characters. Graffiti stays in artwork/wordmark, never behind essential text.
PRODUCT TRUTH: These radio stations are artist/genre-seeded mixes from the user's LOCAL MUSIC LIBRARY. They are not live broadcasts. Use a concise line "Mixes from your library". No FM frequencies, listeners, broadcast schedules, social sharing, fake metrics, ads or subscription upsells.
CONSISTENT SAMPLE CONTENT across all concepts: desktop page title "Radio". Main station "Night Ride" with genres "Electronic · Synthpop"; other stations "Blue Hour" (Ambient), "Side Street" (Hip-hop · Funk), "Soft Static" (Lo-fi), "Neon Breaks" (Breakbeat), "High Voltage" (Rock). A compact input "Find a station", "All genres" filter, and discreet "Manage stations" link. Global navigation only "Library", "Explore", "Radio" with Radio active, and a small settings icon. Use actual station names as typographic UI outside artwork, not baked into poster illustrations.
MOBILE screen is Night Ride station detail: back to Radio, station name/artwork, brief genre labels, one short description "A late-night mix from your library.", a discreet edit icon, "Built from" seeds "Glass Arcade" and "Night Courier". Bottom playback shows fictional current track "Afterimage" by "Glass Arcade". Keep advanced details behind one small menu.
PLAYBACK: One visually dominant play/pause button per screen in a compact persistent playback area, small previous/next, track title/artist, and ONE waveform whose bars form the interactive seek rail with a progress thumb and tiny elapsed/duration at its edges. Waveform IS the seeking bar; never a separate decorative equalizer or extra slider. Desktop may show tiny queue/volume icons; mobile only essential playback and one menu. Do not repeat large play buttons throughout station cards.
CRAFT: bold anime street culture meets highly usable music software; excellent spacing, large tap targets, clean native-feeling mobile layout, upright readable text, clear contrast, sharp functional icons. Typography should feel designed, not default dashboard. Use cool neutrals or deliberate dark surfaces; acid #d7ff3f, cobalt #3b4fd8, orange #ff7144 as disciplined accents. No cream UI, no ornamental all-caps eyebrow labels, no italic emphasis, no floating random sticker chips, no superfluous analytics. Do not put concept numbers into app content.
SPECIFIC STRUCTURAL DIRECTION follows; prioritize it over any layout implied by reference images.

concepts.name: Record shop
concepts.distinction: Six illustrated sleeves make station discovery feel like browsing a record store.
concepts.direction: RECORD SHOP. Desktop uses compact horizontal global nav and a roomy cool-gray canvas. Radio title and search/filter share one tidy header; below is a beautifully spaced 3-column by 2-row GRID of six square illustrated station sleeves, with live station names and genres in clean small text below each sleeve. Night Ride has a quiet acid selection frame, no duplicated play buttons. Avoid a huge page hero. Six distinct original screenprinted anime street-scene artworks: subway skater, foggy bridge, graffiti alley, cassette studio, orange stairwell, punk rehearsal. A minimal persistent bottom player has compact thumbnail, title, integrated waveform seek and one large circular play control. Mobile station-detail is a record sleeve composition: square cover at top with generous cool-white margins, large Night Ride and small genres below, compact seed-artist links, simple bottom player. Tactile record-store editorial design without fake vinyl rotation, knobs or skeuomorphic controls.
concepts.risk: Easy discovery; a large collection will need efficient scrolling and filtering.

concepts.name: Radio zine
concepts.distinction: An editorial spread pairs one featured station with a fast, scannable index.
concepts.direction: RADIO ZINE. Desktop is an editorial independent music zine made into crisp software: big upper-left Radio display title, horizontal nav, fine black rules. Main content ASYMMETRIC: left 60% is a wide landscape anime street scene with Night Ride title set below in enormous condensed black type; right 40% is a sharply aligned vertical index of other stations with small artwork thumbnails and genre labels, separated by hairline rules. Search/filter sit above the index, not over illustration. Large cool-gray negative space but actual station choices visible above fold. Artwork: original anime courier on orange bicycle under cobalt elevated railway, acid sunset, striking screenprint crop. Orange restrained rule and acid active underline. Bottom integrated waveform player feels like a publication footer. Mobile translates the editorial spread into tall artwork, oversized but two-line maximum Night Ride title, simple genre line and seed links, one compact playback area. No overlapping newspaper text, torn-paper unreadability or all-caps metadata.
concepts.risk: Strong hierarchy; the featured station should not hide the rest of the library.

concepts.name: Transit lines
concepts.distinction: A graphic station map explores genre connections, with a clear list alternative.
concepts.direction: TRANSIT LINES. The most experimental but plausible UI: desktop cool-gray main canvas has a clean graphic TRANSIT-DIAGRAM style station selector occupying left two-thirds, using thick cobalt, ink and orange paths, each with large clearly readable labeled station stops, small square art next to each label, six stations total. This is a visual browse layout for genre-seeded stations, not a geographical map, not actual transit or FM frequencies. Above it Radio title, search/filter and "Map / List" toggle with Map selected, assuring an accessible list alternative. Right third is a selected Night Ride card with a fresh original anime train-platform headphone listener artwork, large Night Ride, genres and seed links. Keep connecting lines away from readable text; no confusing numbers, analytics or map zoom controls. Acid accent marks selected Night Ride stop, white/cool-gray label backing. Compact single bottom player. Mobile uses LIST-FIRST browsing convention (small station selector above detail) and a simple Night Ride cover/detail view with a tiny decorative route line beside the two seed links; never shrink the diagram onto phone. Respect simple waveform seek player.
concepts.risk: Most experimental: spatial browsing needs a fully usable list alternative.

concepts.name: Listening desk
concepts.distinction: A steady three-pane workspace puts stations, current artwork and seeds side by side.
concepts.direction: LISTENING DESK. Desktop a disciplined three-pane listening workspace, no dashboard metrics. Narrow left pane station directory with search and six rows; generous central pane selected Night Ride artwork and current-track title; narrow right pane clear station identity, "Electronic · Synthpop", brief local-library explanation, two seed artist links and discreet edit/manage actions. Global navigation a compact top bar. Central anime scene is a original headphone-wearing woman at a rooftop mixing desk with cobalt city blocks, orange speakers and a small acid sky area. Cool-gray surrounding panels, thin ink dividers, restrained acid active state. Artwork appears large and square, not a tiny thumbnail. Bottom center playback is one clear play button, previous/next and integrated waveform seek; no extra EQ graphs, no mixer faders, no sound-engineering clutter. Mobile becomes a single focused listening screen: cover, title and concise genres, seeds collapsed under "Built from", beautifully spacious simple player. This option should feel most practical for long listening sessions while retaining the bold street-radio visual identity.
concepts.risk: Useful while listening; the third pane should collapse cleanly on smaller screens.

concepts.name: Poster wall
concepts.distinction: Tall station posters create a bold horizontal browse experience.
concepts.direction: POSTER WALL. Desktop horizontal illustrated station ribbon below compact title/search/nav: four TALL POSTERS visible at once, the selected Night Ride poster larger/wider and three other station posters narrower, with a hint of next poster at right to suggest horizontal browse. Each poster is framed in thin ink and has station name in a separate cool-gray footer, not in art. Poster art original anime/skate street screenprints with strong differing compositions and common acid/cobalt/orange palette: DJ against towering speaker, dusk stairwell, train graffiti, skate bowl. Selected poster's footer expands with concise genres and seeds; other footers show only name and genre. Single steady bottom playback dock, integrated waveform. Background cool gray, deliberate large display type, no busy masonry/pinterest tiles or labels over illustration. Mobile transforms into ONE full-height Night Ride art poster with white/cool-gray information panel below and short seed list, functional bottom waveform+playback. Striking graphic arts gallery energy with clean interactive structure.
concepts.risk: Artwork leads; keyboard and touch navigation through the ribbon will matter.

concepts.name: Gallery tunnel
